text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Natural calamities have caused major losses for Vietnam in 1996 but economic results are still encouraging.
-- The central State Bank of Vietnam has devised new programmes aimed at improving regulatory and monetary polices while reorganising its managerial apparatus.
-- A brain drain from Vietnam's state sector to foreign and private business is a major problem.

-- Vietnam's judo champion Cao Ngoc Phuong Trinh has underscored her reputation as a top regional martial arts expert by winning a gold medal at the Golden Jubilee International Judo Championships in Bangkok.
-- Oil firm Vietsovpetro expects crude oil output this year to reach a target of 8.2 million tonnes, a rise of 22 percent.
-- Police throughout Vietnam have seized 3,000 illegal guns in the past three months.
-- Vice President Nguyen Thi Binh and China's visiting Party Central Committee member, Qi Huai Yuan, have discussed ways to increase cooperation and improve ties.
-- 570,000 hectares of sugar cane have been completely destroyed by natural calamities this year.
